transcript:
Meeting header: Date: 2027-10-20 15:00 UTC
Duration: 57 min
Attendees: Jordan Miles (Redwood AE), Priya Desai (Redwood SE), Evan Park (SynthTech ML Lead), Lara Chen (SynthTech Infra), Marcus O'Neil (CTO)

[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone, thanks for joining we want to cover the quantization tradeoffs - int8, fp8, gptq, awq and how they affect latency throughput and accuracy on your workloads
[00:08] Evan: yeah thanks, we're especially worried about any accuracy regressions on our customer prompts, we run a lot of few-shot prompts with long context and a warmed up KV cache
[00:15] Priya: quick question on stack - what's your production runtime? are you on K8s with private VPC, are you looking hosted or dedicated?
[00:22] Lara: we are on a hybrid setup - prod runs in our VPC on dedicated nodes for now, but we are evaluating on-prem in air-gap mode later this year. SSO and KMS are requirements
[00:30] Jordan: cool, that pushed us towards looking closely at AWQ and GPTQ as they give different perf/accuracy tradeoffs for on-prem flows
[00:38] Priya: high level: INT8 (quant-aware or calibration based) typically gives best latency but can incur regressions, FP8 often preserves quality but hardware support is limited, GPTQ/AWQ are post-training quantization techniques that trade off per-layer accuracy vs model size.
[00:50] Evan: can you expand on AWQ vs GPTQ? we've seen a paper that AWQ produced smaller models but sometimes had 'outlier' token probs shift
[00:58] Priya: sure. GPTQ does matrix-wise quantization with per-channel scales and often uses block-wise fine-tuning (approx) - it can preserve perplexity but is heavier to generate; AWQ (Adaptive Weight Quantization) focuses on asymmetric quantization and activation-aware calibration, tends to be faster and smaller but can introduce small distribution shifts that affect classification logits
[01:15] Marcus: how does this interact with our KV cache? our application uses long context and prefix caching heavily, we don't want first-token penalties or cache mismatch behavior
[01:22] Priya: good point. KV cache is purely runtime memory of activations/keys; quantization affects the forward pass and the produced keys/values. Small shifts in weights can produce drift in KV vectors which means cached prefixes might not match exactly, leading to slightly different continuation. In practice we've seen warm cache reduces regressions because most of the heavy work is token generation not initial state, but there are corner cases
[01:40] Evan: are there mitigation techniques? we can't afford hallucination increases
[01:44] Priya: strategies: 1) selective quantization: keep attention/LayerNorm/embedding layers in fp16 while quantizing MLPs; 2) per-channel calibration and outlier handling - clipping or outlier-aware scale; 3) mixed-precision fallback for sensitive tokens; 4) run small eval set to detect distributional shift and choose profile
[02:05] Jordan: on the runtime side, for latency we look at kernel selection - INT8 kernels are highly optimized on some runtimes but FP8/FP16 kernels can be much faster on newer GPUs if natively supported. Also batching: continuous batching helps throughput but raises tail latency; Redwood's runtime supports dynamic batching and per-route SLOs
[02:25] Lara: our infra question: can we deploy these quantized models inside our VPC with HSM keys and no egress? also any extra telemetry we need?
[02:32] Jordan: yes Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS/HSM and air-gapped deploys; we can disable telemetry or drop identifiers; for benchmarking we'll need a small agent to run locally - it's compatible with air-gapped setups
[02:40] Priya: back to accuracy: we ran internal benchmarks on three models similar to yours (13b, 30b, 70b). Results summary: GPTQ often preserved accuracy within 1-2% on LLM evals, AWQ gave 0.5-1.5% degradation on average but better latency and smaller memory. INT8 with naive calibration caused 2-5% regressions on instruction-following tests unless we selectively excluded LayerNorm and embeddings
[03:05] Evan: can you give numbers on latency improvements?
[03:08] Priya: roughs: on same GPU, INT8 (well-tuned) reduced per-token latency by ~20-30% vs fp16, AWQ gave ~15-25% and GPTQ varied (depends on kernel support) - sometimes GPTQ quantized ops run slower due to lack of fused kernels but memory bandwidth reduced so throughput increases in high-batch scenarios
[03:30] Marcus: what about memory / kv cache size changes?
[03:33] Priya: quantized weights are smaller (4x for int8 vs fp32), kv cache is still activation precision dependent - if you keep activations in fp16 the kv cache doesn't shrink as much. AWQ/GPTQ mainly reduce model weight memory; if we quantize activations too you can shrink cache but risk more numeric issues
[03:52] Evan: our biggest worry is regression on our safety classifier triggers - false positives/negatives change with quantization and that breaks safety SLAs
[03:58] Priya: we recommend a two-stage approach: first run offline evals (your 5k prompts) to measure delta across metrics (safety classifier scores, top-k prob shifts), second run a short live pilot with traffic shadowing and A/B compare outputs, plus automatic rollback if delta exceeds threshold
[04:20] Jordan: question on tooling: we have a small 'eval harness' that can run exact-diff checks and compute token-level KL divergence and ROC changes, we can run that against your set and produce per-model reports
[04:31] Evan: great, can you run AWQ and GPTQ and show per-prompt diffs, not just aggregate? some prompts are business-critical
[04:37] Priya: yep we'll produce per-prompt diffs. we'll also attach failure examples where top-1 changes or safety classifier flips.
[04:45] Lara: about pilot infra: what does Redwood need to run benchmarks on our nodes? network, container, GPU driver versions?
[04:51] Jordan: we need container runtime (docker or containerd), CUDA and driver compat (we'll provide a spec), and minimal outbound for license if not air-gapped - for air-gapped we provide signed images and offline install instructions. We'll also share a checklist for KMS/HSM integration
[05:05] Marcus: any gotchas on model conversion? we are using a custom tokenizer and some fine-tuned adapters
[05:11] Priya: tokens: quantization shouldn't change tokenizer outputs; problems arise if adapter weights are small magnitude causing larger relative quantization noise. For adapters, we sometimes keep them in fp16 or apply per-adapter scaling. We'll validate during conversion step
[05:26] Evan: curious about FP8 - you said limited hardware support, but our upcoming infra might have next-gen cards
[05:31] Priya: FP8 (e4m3/e5m2) can give good dynamic range and preserve accuracy, but tooling around calibration and stable kernels is still maturing; if your GPUs support it and driver stack is compatible we can run experiments. FP8 often needs special fused kernels for best perf
[05:45] Jordan: ok let's talk concrete plan: Priya will run GPTQ + AWQ + INT8-selected on your eval set (13b & 30b) and produce per-prompt diffs, latency/throughput numbers, and recommended config. We'll run these inside your VPC with the minimal agent. Evan will share eval set. Jordan will send the infra checklist and pricing for pilot
[06:05] Evan: timeline? we want results in about 2 weeks
[06:08] Priya: 2 weeks is reasonable for 2 models and the eval set size you mentioned, assuming GPUs available. We'll record exact runtimes and produce a short report
[06:15] Lara: security review: we need SOC2 docs and network diagrams before infra access
[06:20] Jordan: we'll send SOC2 and security pack with architecture diagrams; for on-prem we'll add our air-gap instructions and references to audit logs options
[06:30] Marcus: any notes about batching - we rely on low tail latency for interactive sessions, batching can help throughput but hurts tails
[06:36] Priya: Redwood runtime supports per-route batch caps and low-latency mode where we favor single request latency over throughput; also prefix KV caching reduces compute for repeated prefixes. We can also tune micro-batching (max batch size 4-8) and scheduling windows to balance SLOs
[06:55] Evan: can you share sample benchmarks that show tail latency vs throughput curves?
[06:58] Priya: yes we'll include P95/P99 curves for each quantization profile and different batch sizes in the report
[07:10] Jordan: ok I'm going to recap next steps and owners...
[07:14] Jordan: recap: Priya run benchmarks (GPTQ, AWQ, INT8-selective) on 13b & 30b -> deliver per-prompt diffs, latency, P95/P99 curves; Evan share eval set and any safety thresholds; Jordan send infra checklist and pricing; schedule follow-up in two weeks
[07:32] Evan: sounds good, thanks
[07:34] Lara: thanks everyone
[07:36] Marcus: appreciate it
[07:38] Priya: thanks, talk soon

End of transcript.
